questions.problem:
| ${x}_{1}$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${x}_{2}$ | **$8$** | **$15$** | **$29$** | **$22$** | **$41$** |
| $y$ | $0$ | $-10$ | $-6$ | $5$ | $11$ |

The vector of coefficients of the plane $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}{x}_{1}+{\beta }_{2}{x}_{2}$ that best fits the data above can be found using multiple linear regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?
questions.worked_solution:
| ${x}_{1}$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${x}_{2}$ | **$8$** | **$15$** | **$29$** | **$22$** | **$41$** |
| $y$ | $0$ | $-10$ | $-6$ | $5$ | $11$ |

The coefficients of the plane 

$$
y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}{x}_{1}+{\beta }_{2}{x}_{2}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 8 \\ 1 & 2 & 15 \\ 1 & 3 & 29 \\ 1 & 4 & 22 \\ 1 & 5 & 41\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -10 \\ -6 \\ 5 \\ 11\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

The coefficients of the hyperplane  

$$
y= \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 x_2 +\beta_3 x_3
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution ${\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}}$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & -8 & 8 \\ 2 & -2 & 6 \\ 3 & 6 & 4 \\ 4 & 15 & 2\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 20 \\ 40 \\ 60\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\boldsymbol{\beta}$ is the parameter vector, and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector.
